title: Joints
objective: After this level you can name the main kinds of joint and explain how they let us move.
summary: A joint is where bones meet. Some never move (skull sutures), some move a little (between vertebrae), and synovial joints move freely, cushioned by cartilage and slick fluid.

cards.headline: Some of your joints never move. That's the point.
cards.body: A joint is anywhere two bones meet. Your knee bends, your shoulder swings in a circle, and the joints in your skull barely move at all. Same word, very different jobs.

cards.headline: Three kinds of joint, sorted by movement

items.label: Immovable
points: Sutures lock the skull's bones together
Their job is protecting the brain

items.label: Slightly movable
points: The discs between the vertebrae of your spine

items.label: Freely movable
points: Synovial joints, such as the knee, hip and elbow

cards.headline: Why a knee doesn't grind
cards.body: Freely movable joints share one clever design. The bone ends are capped with smooth cartilage and sealed inside a capsule. The capsule's lining makes synovial fluid, a thick, slippery liquid that lubricates the joint and cuts friction between the bones. Every time you bend a knee, cartilage glides over cartilage on a thin slick of fluid.

items.label: Hinge
points: Bend and straighten along one line, like a door

items.label: Pivot
points: Rotates, so you can turn your head

items.label: Ball-and-socket
points: Hip and shoulder, the only two
The widest range of motion of any joint

cards.headline: Joints: in motion
learned: A joint is where two bones meet
Immovable, slightly movable and freely movable joints
Synovial joints: cartilage caps and slippery synovial fluid
Hinge, pivot and ball-and-socket shapes move differently

questions.prompt: Which two joints are the body's only ball-and-socket joints?

options.label: The top two vertebrae
options.rationale: That's a pivot joint for turning the head.

questions.explanation: The hip and shoulder are the only ball-and-socket joints, and they have the widest range of motion.

questions.prompt: What does synovial fluid do inside a freely movable joint?

options.label: Locks the bones so they can't move
options.rationale: That describes immovable sutures, not synovial joints.

options.label: Lubricates the joint and reduces friction
Makes new blood cells
options.rationale: Blood cells come from red marrow.

options.label: Hardens the ends of the bones
options.rationale: The bone ends are capped with smooth cartilage.

questions.explanation: Synovial fluid is a thick, slippery fluid that lubricates the joint and reduces friction between the bones.

questions.prompt: Level 11's axial skeleton protects the brain. What kind of joint holds the skull's bones together?

options.label: A ball-and-socket joint
options.rationale: Only the hip and shoulder have those.

options.label: A hinge joint
options.rationale: Hinges bend, like the elbow and knee.

options.label: A pivot joint
options.rationale: The pivot sits between the top two vertebrae.

questions.explanation: The skull's bones are joined by sutures, immovable joints that help protect the brain.
